title: Simulation of one register-program step
statement: Let $A$ be a register program with $m$ registers and access to $d$ Boolean oracles, and let $D$ be a machine with $k_D$ work tapes and designated initial states $q_0(j)$. Suppose one abstract step from the active configuration with control state $l$, register values $v$, and no stored answer yields the active configuration with state $l'$, values $v'$, and no stored answer. Suppose the starting configuration satisfies the precondition for $A$, and for every register $r$ the bit length of $v(r)+1$ is at most $W$. Then the compiled machine, started in the seam configuration encoding $l$, $v$, and output word $out$, reaches the seam configuration encoding $l'$, $v'$, and the same output word after some finite number $T$ of steps; at every earlier time $t<T$, its configuration satisfies the stated invariant for $A$, $l_0$, $B$, and $W$.
hypotheses_covered: The one-step abstract transition equation from (l, v, none) to (l', v', none)
